title: Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0045】In this review, we investigate the application of AI to address these challenges, leveraging the most advanced techniques such as complex models and high-performance LLMs. AI-driven diagnostics can reduce reliance on empiric therapy by enabling rapid pathogen identification and resistance prediction. In treatment, AI methods, including protein language models like ESM-2, expedite the development of novel antibiotics and alternative therapies. For decision-making, LLMs integrate multimodal data to support personalized treatment choices and policy formulation. However, strong predictive performance alone does not establish the clinical value of AI applications in AMR. We therefore use a five-stage translational framework to distinguish proof-of-concept performance from clinical utility (Fig. 1B). The stages comprise computational validation, external validation, prospective clinical validation, implementation evaluation, and demonstrated clinical or public-health impact. The distinctive contribution of this review is to connect traditionally separated AI applications across AMR within a unified framework based on data modality and translational stage from a One Health perspective. Rather than considering these applications in isolation, we examine how multimodal data are processed by AI to support resistance detection, antimicrobial discovery, clinical decision-making, and surveillance. Particular attention is given to foundation models and language-model-based approaches that bridge sequence interpretation, therapeutic generation, and knowledge-guided decision support. This cross-scale perspective enables us to assess not only computational advances but also the evidence required for their clinical and public-health translation.

【Introduction · p0030】Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is the evolving process by which bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites develop resistance to medicines previously effective against them. According to the most recent Global Burden of Disease analysis, bacterial AMR was directly responsible for 1.14 million global deaths in 2021 and contributed to a total of 4.71 million deaths. Without effective intervention, drug-resistant bacterial infections could lead to 8.22 million deaths globally in 2050, with a particularly heavy toll expected in South Asia and Latin America and the Caribbean [1].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Discovery and design of candidate AMP for antimicrobial treatment · p0160】Large-scale metagenomic studies demonstrate the scalability of AI-based AMP mining. Ma et al. developed a computational pipeline for candidate AMP screening using human gut microbiome data, incorporating natural language processing models such as LSTM [34], Attention [35], and BERT [36], [37]. The researchers trained an AMP prediction model based on four public databases: ADAM, APD, CAMP, and LAMP. For AMP mining, the prediction model was applied to 11,011 metagenomes, leading to the identification of 2349 candidate AMPs. Among 216 peptides chemically synthesized, over 83% exhibited high antimicrobial activity, as confirmed by experimental validation. Santos-Júnior et al. subsequently used Macrel to screen 63,410 metagenomes from diverse habitats [38]. This analysis generated AMPSphere, which contains 863,498 non-redundant peptides, most of which were absent from existing databases [39].

【Discovery and design of candidate AMP for antimicrobial treatment · p0170】A species-aware, peptide-tuned ESM-2 model was developed for AMP identification through pre-training on 1.7 million peptides. During fine-tuning, the embeddings generated by the peptide-tuned ESM-2 were integrated with genomic features from 45 different species to learn species-specific peptide activities and MIC values [44]. This species-aware approach enhances the efficiency of AMP design and screening processes tailored to particular species.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【AI-enhanced diagnosis of antimicrobial resistance · p0075】AI with established diagnostic methodologies significantly enhances efficiency and accuracy in antimicrobial resistance detection. Advancements in AI, particularly DL, have augmented conventional approaches. CNNs, attention-based architectures, and BERT-derived models can predict putative ARGs with limited sequence similarity to known resistance genes, thereby expanding the pool of candidates for experimental validation. Concurrently, LLMs support clinical decision-making by processing multimodal inputs, including electronic medical records, sequence data, medical images, lab results, and clinical guidelines.

【AI for rapid molecular diagnosis · p0080】The main determinants of AMR are the ARGs. The traditional method is based on alignment with ARG datasets like CARD [6], ARDB [7], ResFinder [8] and AMRFinder [9]. The limitation of methods based on alignment is that only ARGs present in the database can be detected; novel ARGs cannot be identified by sequence matching alone. After training with the sequence of the existing datasets, AI can solve the problem and find candidate ARG.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · f0005】Fig. 1 The figure illustrates a hierarchical AI framework and its translational framework from proof of concept to real-world impact in AMR research. (A) Machine learning comprises conventional methods, such as logistic regression, random forests, and support vector machines, as well as deep learning. Deep-learning architectures include CNNs and Transformers, with the latter encompassing BERT-derived architectures, protein language models, and LLMs. Generative AI enables new content generation, whereas RAG augments model outputs with information retrieved from external knowledge sources. (B) AI technologies require progressive evidence generation, moving from computational and external validation to prospective evaluation, implementation, and demonstrated clinical or public-health benefit. Similarly, AI-assisted antimicrobial discovery requires validation beyond in silico prediction, including experimental, preclinical, and clinical assessment. CNN, convolutional neural network; LLM, large language model; ML, machine learning; RAG, retrieval-augmented generation.

【Fig. 2 · f0010】Fig. 2 The figure provides an overview of three advanced diagnostic technologies that utilize machine learning and data analysis for the rapid detection and characterization of AMR. (A) DhLSI; (B) Raman spectroscopy; (C) MALDI-TOF. DhLSI, dynamic holographic laser speckle imaging; MALDI-TOF, matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight.

【Fig. 3 · f0015】Fig. 3 The figure illustrates the process of molecule representation for AI. It shows how a chemical structure (top) is translated into different data formats that can be processed by AI. Text String Representation: Molecules are encoded as text. SMILES use a string of characters to describe the molecule's connectivity. Molecular fingerprints represent the presence or absence of specific substructures as a binary vector. 2D Model Representation: A molecule is treated as a graph, where atoms are nodes and bonds are edges. This representation captures the topological structure of the molecule. 3D Model Representation: This method captures the molecule's three-dimensional spatial arrangement. The coordinates of each atom (x, y, z) are stored in a matrix, providing a more detailed view of the molecule's shape and conformation. These representations can serve as inputs to AI models such as Transformers, graph neural networks, 3D CNNs, variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, and diffusion models. SMILES, Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System; CNN, convolutional neural network.

【AI-enhanced diagnosis of antimicrobial resistance · p0060】To combat antimicrobial resistance (AMR), diagnostics—particularly rapid diagnostics—play a pivotal role. Conventional phenotypic methods, such as antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) and MIC determination, remain the gold standard. However, these approaches are time-consuming due to reliance on pure cultures and provide limited insight into the mechanisms underlying resistance.
